key_insight: A genome-guided, physics-informed screening framework can rapidly identify phase-stable, lead-free double perovskites by using interpretable descriptors tied to structure, bonding, and optoelectronic behavior.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical inverse design of safer semiconductor absorbers and sensor materials with DFT-validated candidates that are more likely to be synthesizable and optoelectronically useful.
method: Built surrogate models from 1,221 DFT-calculated A2BB'X6 compounds using four descriptor families: packing, bonding, polarization, and electronic identity.
Applied a staged inverse-design filter to 13,088 charge-balanced compositions to narrow the search to five DFT-validated stable candidates.
Used machine learning for stability classification and band-gap regression, then verified final materials with DFT and convex-hull analysis.
evidence_signal: The stability classifier reached ROC-AUC = 0.92 and the XGBoost band-gap model achieved R2 = 0.93 on held-out data, while the final five candidates all satisfied E_hull <= 0 meV/atom.
watch_item: The workflow depends on DFT-trained surrogates and composition space coverage, so performance may weaken for chemistries outside the training distribution or under experimental synthesis constraints.
paper_title: Genome-Guided Interpretable Screening of Phase-Stable, Lead-Free Double Perovskite Absorbers for All-Inorganic Semiconductors, Sensors, and Photovoltaics with DFT-Validated Design Rules
